AETHERFORGE — V12 / STRONGER BIOSHOCK 1 AND 2 CONCEPT-ART DIRECTION
This revision responds to two user critiques: previous sheets looked too realistic and generically AI-polished; the angular gouache revision still needs substantially more of the artistic language of BioShock 1 and BioShock 2. Create genuine ORIGINAL hand-painted game concept art. Repaint and redesign the forms, do not apply a surface filter and do not paste reference pixels.

STYLE: early BioShock concept-sheet sensibility: theatrical adult caricature, slightly ungainly proportions, crooked noses, asymmetrical tired faces, long thin limbs beside heavy compact bodies, expressive occupational gesture. Hand-drawn curved silhouettes and selective dark contours, painterly local-color washes, soft economical modeling inside bold shapes. Linework may be searching and slightly uneven. A few carefully resolved focal details surrounded by simpler painted cloth and shadow. Drawn personality and grotesque industrial melancholy, never cosmetic beauty or heroic posing. LESS naturalistic than the old v11 paintings, but not cubist, faceted low-poly, flat vector, chibi, cute cartoon, smooth Disney-like character, anime, photorealistic costume, glossy CGI/PBR render, cinematic poster or generic hyperdetailed steampunk. Avoid broad polygonal planes everywhere. Avoid repeating the same handsome face. No pores, individual fabric fibers, bloom, rim-light, oily metallic shine, all-over tiny rust scratches, greebles or procedural-looking noise.

DESIGN CULTURE: 1930s–40s institutional working clothes and mass-produced industrial products, once-dignified Art Deco designs patched by ordinary workers. Long coats with real tailoring, short work jackets, enamel and leather with different jobs. Simple stepped edges, vertical ribs, tapered casings and a few chunky visible fasteners. Every large form has a purpose. Painterly curved metal has weight without rendering a thousand rivets. Maintain ORIGINAL Brumaferrea terrestrial industrial fantasy, not underwater Rapture. No recognizable franchise character, logo, Big Daddy/Big Sister helmet, cage, drill, ADAM bottle face, Little Sister, bird mask or copied weapon. The supplied franchise art is a reference for drawing, gesture and functional material hierarchy, not content to copy.

COLOR: preserve the accepted warm v10 family. Warm archive putty #BFB49E background; soot #241F1A, tobacco #40332B, OXBLOOD enamel #6C3A32, restrained aged brass #B99B63, old linen/porcelain #E4D8B7, tiny muted jade #97A581 only when needed. Distinct oxblood and linen color masses, not a uniform brown tint. Quiet nearly uniform paper background, no vignette, no blue/teal field, cyan/gold lighting, fog, neon or dramatic background scenery. Minimal painted ground shadows. No decorative gears. One small three-rib split-arch seam may unify original equipment, no repeated emblems.

COMPOSITION: one horizontal landscape concept sheet, preferably 16:9 at native supported resolution. Exactly THREE separate subjects in the prescribed order, whole bodies, all extremities and tools visible, at least a clear paper margin on every side including above heads. Similar editorial presence rather than identical world scale. No second views, inset faces, extra figures, text, captions, numbers, letters, signature, credits, logo, UI, frames or ornamental borders in the generated painting. Keep full-body tool grips and purposeful load-bearing joints readable. Deliver PAINTING with visible authored drawing decisions, not a photoreal render or procedural maquette.

IMAGE ROLES: Image 1 is the current original Aetherforge team: preserve the three occupational identities and warm palette but replace its faceted/triangulated drawing with more organic theatrical BioShock-like concept drawing. Image 2 is BioShock 1 citizens research: use ONLY adult caricature, distinctive period tailoring, slumped occupational gesture and economical drawn faces; do not copy any character, clothing arrangement, wounds, disease or pose. Image 3 is BioShock 2 equipment-hand research: use ONLY the illustrative integration of cloth, leather and purposeful industrial product shapes; do not reproduce the glove, its mechanisms, symbols or typography.

G01 — TEAM, LEFT TO RIGHT:
GUNSLINGER: adult woman railway inspector, short dark period bob, long weary asymmetrical exposed face with expressive nose and brow. Tall narrow tobacco coat with TWO large tailored skirt panels, ONE broad ivory diagonal inspection sash. Practical approximately horizontal pressure rifle with wood stock, ONE thick stepped brass receiver, black barrel, both hands touching it correctly. Thin silhouette and workwear, not armored adventurer, top hat or beauty-model pose. One utility pouch is enough.
BOILER GUARD: older human worker with small tired broad face under a COMPACT angular industrial helmet. A short-necked broad trapezius, barrel-chested stout silhouette, heavy hands/boots and awkward burdened stance. Soot work armor with ONE dark oxblood chest plate; FLAT rectangular rear pressure pack, no cylinders above shoulders. SHORT maintenance hammer in one hand. Large RECTANGULAR shield, parallel long sides, beveled corners, exactly ONE chipped ochre VERTICAL stripe; not a coffin, pointed medieval shield or hatch. Human face clearly visible, no diving helmet/porthole. Simple functional articulation rather than layers of fantasy armor.
ETHER ALCHEMIST: ADULT field medic with an unmistakably mature, slightly gaunt kind face; stooped careful posture, not child or young glamorous model. Old-linen hood and cape create a broad triangular silhouette, warm gray work trousers, one canvas medical satchel, exactly ONE small dull jade cartridge integrated into a compact brass hand applicator. Both hands carefully working with the applicator, no extra green vials, giant syringe or medical icon. A medic's practical cape, never nun costume or Little Sister reference.
Maintain exactly these three, no overlap between rifle and guard, clear gaps, big paper margins. Make the people feel like specific tired citizens who volunteered for an expedition. Keep the guard's physique recognizably human, not a miniature Big Daddy.

SOOT RAT: sinister unmistakably RODENT-shaped low horizontal animal, pointed wedge snout, small round ears, tense powerful bent hind legs, long THIN curved tail wholly in frame. ONLY TWO OR THREE small dull mineral ether deposits half-buried in the back fur; no row of spikes, armor, boar body or hedgehog outline. Strong horizontal silhouette.
MECHANICAL SCAVENGER: abandoned salvage automaton with narrow leaning ribbed torso, sloping small mechanical head and short work apron of several large overlapping pressure plates. PATROL DRONE: compact warning-BELL body hanging below TWO lateral SHROUDED ROTORS. The two rotor rings are clearly readable, one at each side, broad horizontal silhouette and pendant central inverted bell skirt, single SMALL downward lens. Suspended well above its painted ground shadow, no legs, no quadcopter, flying eye or cute expression. A vintage institutional machine, subtly tapered Art Deco casings and soot/oxblood/ochre, not shiny gold all over.
